formulas.title: Basic Percentage Definition
formulas.note: Converts a percentage P into a fraction of 100 multiplied by base value X.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount basic percentage definition p% of x = (p / 100) * x converts a percentage p into a fraction of 100 multiplied by base value x. p\% \text{ of } x = \frac{p}{100} \times x

formulas.title: Percentage Share
formulas.note: Expresses one quantity as a percentage of the total reference quantity.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount percentage share percentage = (part / whole) * 100% expresses one quantity as a percentage of the total reference quantity. \text{percentage} = \left(\frac{\text{part}}{\text{whole}}\right) \times 100\%

formulas.title: Percentage Change
formulas.note: Denominator is always the original value V_old. Positive indicates increase; negative indicates decrease.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount percentage change percent change = ((v_new - v_old) / v_old) * 100% denominator is always the original value v_old. positive indicates increase; negative indicates decrease. \delta\% = \left(\frac{v_{\text{new}} - v_{\text{old}}}{v_{\text{old}}}\right) \times 100\%

formulas.title: Value After Percentage Increase
formulas.note: Direct multiplier for increasing an initial quantity V_0 by r%.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount value after percentage increase v_final = v_0 * (1 + r / 100) direct multiplier for increasing an initial quantity v_0 by r%. v_{\text{final}} = v_{0}\left(1 + \frac{r}{100}\right)

formulas.title: Value After Percentage Decrease
formulas.note: Direct multiplier for reducing an initial quantity V_0 by r%.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount value after percentage decrease v_final = v_0 * (1 - r / 100) direct multiplier for reducing an initial quantity v_0 by r%. v_{\text{final}} = v_{0}\left(1 - \frac{r}{100}\right)

formulas.title: Reverse Percentage (Original Value)
formulas.note: Recovers the original pre-change value when only the final value and rate r% are known.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount reverse percentage (original value) v_0 = v_final / (1 +/- r / 100) recovers the original pre-change value when only the final value and rate r% are known. v_{0} = \frac{v_{\text{final}}}{1 \pm \frac{r}{100}}

formulas.title: Successive Percentage Change (Two Steps)
formulas.note: Use negative sign for decreases. Applies when two percentage changes a% and b% occur sequentially.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount successive percentage change (two steps) net % = (a + b + (a * b) / 100)% use negative sign for decreases. applies when two percentage changes a% and b% occur sequentially. \text{net }\% = \left(a + b + \frac{ab}{100}\right)\%

formulas.title: Equal Increase then Decrease by r%
formulas.note: Increasing a number by r% and then decreasing by r% always results in a net decrease of (r^2 / 100)%.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount equal increase then decrease by r% net change = -(r^2 / 100)% increasing a number by r% and then decreasing by r% always results in a net decrease of (r^2 / 100)%. \text{net change} = -\left(\frac{r^{2}}{100}\right)\%

formulas.title: Offsetting Percentage Reduction After r% Rise
formulas.note: If price rises by r%, consumption must drop by this percentage to keep total expenditure unchanged.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount offsetting percentage reduction after r% rise required decrease = (r / (100 + r)) * 100% if price rises by r%, consumption must drop by this percentage to keep total expenditure unchanged. \text{required decrease} = \left(\frac{r}{100 + r}\times 100\right)\%

formulas.title: Offsetting Percentage Increase After r% Drop
formulas.note: If price falls by r%, consumption can increase by this percentage without changing expenditure.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount offsetting percentage increase after r% drop required increase = (r / (100 - r)) * 100% if price falls by r%, consumption can increase by this percentage without changing expenditure. \text{required increase} = \left(\frac{r}{100 - r}\times 100\right)\%

formulas.title: Profit Percentage on Cost Price
formulas.note: Profit and loss percentages are always computed with respect to Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount profit percentage on cost price profit % = ((sp - cp) / cp) * 100% profit and loss percentages are always computed with respect to cost price (cp) unless stated otherwise. \text{profit }\% = \left(\frac{\text{sp} - \text{cp}}{\text{cp}}\right) \times 100\%

formulas.title: Selling Price from Profit/Loss Rate
formulas.note: Use +p for profit percentage and -p for loss percentage.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount selling price from profit/loss rate sp = cp * (1 +/- p / 100) use +p for profit percentage and -p for loss percentage. \text{sp} = \text{cp}\left(1 \pm \frac{p}{100}\right)

formulas.title: Discount Percentage on Marked Price
formulas.note: Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) or List Price.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount discount percentage on marked price discount % = ((mp - sp) / mp) * 100% discount is always calculated on the marked price (mp) or list price. \text{discount }\% = \left(\frac{\text{mp} - \text{sp}}{\text{mp}}\right) \times 100\%

formulas.title: Equivalent Single Discount for Two Discounts
formulas.note: Single effective discount rate corresponding to successive discounts d1% and d2%.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount equivalent single discount for two discounts d_eq = (d1 + d2 - (d1 * d2) / 100)% single effective discount rate corresponding to successive discounts d1% and d2%. d_{\text{eq}} = \left(d_{1} + d_{2} - \frac{d_{1}d_{2}}{100}\right)\%

formulas.title: Marked Price to Cost Price Ratio
formulas.note: Directly relates Marked Price and Cost Price when both discount % and profit % are known.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount marked price to cost price ratio mp / cp = (100 + profit%) / (100 - discount%) directly relates marked price and cost price when both discount % and profit % are known. \frac{\text{mp}}{\text{cp}} = \frac{100 + \text{profit }\%}{100 - \text{discount }\%}

formulas.title: Compound Growth / Population Formula
formulas.note: Gives value after n compounding periods at constant growth rate r% per period.
formulas.search_text: percentages percent change · successive change · reverse percentage · profit & discount compound growth / population formula p_n = p_0 * (1 + r / 100)^n gives value after n compounding periods at constant growth rate r% per period. p_{n} = p_{0}\left(1 + \frac{r}{100}\right)^{n}

formulas.title: Definition of Logarithm
formulas.note: Fundamental equivalence between logarithmic form and exponential form.
formulas.search_text: logarithms laws of logarithms · change of base · exponential equivalence · characteristic & mantissa definition of logarithm log_b(x) = y <=> b^y = x (b > 0, b != 1, x > 0) fundamental equivalence between logarithmic form and exponential form. \log_{b}(x) = y \iff b^{y} = x \quad (b > 0,\, b \neq 1,\, x > 0)

formulas.title: Logarithm of Unity and Base
formulas.note: For any valid base b, the log of 1 is 0 and the log of the base itself is 1.
formulas.search_text: logarithms laws of logarithms · change of base · exponential equivalence · characteristic & mantissa logarithm of unity and base log_b(1) = 0, log_b(b) = 1 for any valid base b, the log of 1 is 0 and the log of the base itself is 1. \log_{b}(1) = 0, \qquad \log_{b}(b) = 1

formulas.title: Product Rule of Logarithms
formulas.note: The logarithm of a product equals the sum of the logarithms of its factors (M, N > 0).
formulas.search_text: logarithms laws of logarithms · change of base · exponential equivalence · characteristic & mantissa product rule of logarithms log_b(m * n) = log_b(m) + log_b(n) the logarithm of a product equals the sum of the logarithms of its factors (m, n > 0). \log_{b}(mn) = \log_{b}(m) + \log_{b}(n)

formulas.title: Quotient Rule of Logarithms
formulas.note: The logarithm of a quotient equals the difference of the numerator and denominator logarithms.
formulas.search_text: logarithms laws of logarithms · change of base · exponential equivalence · characteristic & mantissa quotient rule of logarithms log_b(m / n) = log_b(m) - log_b(n) the logarithm of a quotient equals the difference of the numerator and denominator logarithms. \log_{b}\!\left(\frac{m}{n}\right) = \log_{b}(m) - \log_{b}(n)

formulas.title: Power Rule of Argument
formulas.note: An exponent on the argument moves out as a linear multiplier.
formulas.search_text: logarithms laws of logarithms · change of base · exponential equivalence · characteristic & mantissa power rule of argument log_b(m^k) = k * log_b(m) an exponent on the argument moves out as a linear multiplier. \log_{b}\!\left(m^{k}\right) = k\,\log_{b}(m)

formulas.title: Power Rule of Base
formulas.note: An exponent m in the base divides the resulting logarithm while argument exponent n multiplies it.
formulas.search_text: logarithms laws of logarithms · change of base · exponential equivalence · characteristic & mantissa power rule of base log_(b^m)(m^n) = (n / m) * log_b(m) an exponent m in the base divides the resulting logarithm while argument exponent n multiplies it. \log_{b^{m}}\!(m^{n}) = \frac{n}{m}\,\log_{b}(m)

formulas.title: Change of Base Formula
formulas.note: Converts a logarithm from base b to any convenient base c such as 10 or e.
formulas.search_text: logarithms laws of logarithms · change of base · exponential equivalence · characteristic & mantissa change of base formula log_b(a) = log_c(a) / log_c(b) = ln(a) / ln(b) converts a logarithm from base b to any convenient base c such as 10 or e. \log_{b}(a) = \frac{\log_{c}(a)}{\log_{c}(b)} = \frac{\ln(a)}{\ln(b)}

formulas.title: Reciprocal Base Identity
formulas.note: Swapping the base and argument takes the reciprocal of the logarithm.
formulas.search_text: logarithms laws of logarithms · change of base · exponential equivalence · characteristic & mantissa reciprocal base identity log_b(a) = 1 / log_a(b) swapping the base and argument takes the reciprocal of the logarithm. \log_{b}(a) = \frac{1}{\log_{a}(b)} \implies \log_{b}(a)\cdot\log_{a}(b) = 1

formulas.title: Telescoping Chain Rule
formulas.note: Intermediate bases cancel in a chain product of logarithms.
formulas.search_text: logarithms laws of logarithms · change of base · exponential equivalence · characteristic & mantissa telescoping chain rule log_a(b) * log_b(c) * log_c(d) = log_a(d) intermediate bases cancel in a chain product of logarithms. \log_{a}(b)\cdot\log_{b}(c)\cdot\log_{c}(d) = \log_{a}(d)

formulas.title: Inverse Exponential Identity
formulas.note: Exponentiation and logarithms with the same base are inverse operations.
formulas.search_text: logarithms laws of logarithms · change of base · exponential equivalence · characteristic & mantissa inverse exponential identity b^(log_b(x)) = x, log_b(b^x) = x exponentiation and logarithms with the same base are inverse operations. b^{\log_{b}(x)} = x, \qquad \log_{b}\!\left(b^{x}\right) = x

formulas.title: Base-Swapping Exponent Identity
formulas.note: The base a of the power and the argument c inside the exponent logarithm can be interchanged.
formulas.search_text: logarithms laws of logarithms · change of base · exponential equivalence · characteristic & mantissa base-swapping exponent identity a^(log_b(c)) = c^(log_b(a)) the base a of the power and the argument c inside the exponent logarithm can be interchanged. a^{\log_{b}(c)} = c^{\log_{b}(a)}

formulas.title: Reciprocal Base Sign Rule
formulas.note: Replacing the base or argument by its reciprocal negates the logarithm.
formulas.search_text: logarithms laws of logarithms · change of base · exponential equivalence · characteristic & mantissa reciprocal base sign rule log_(1/b)(x) = -log_b(x) = log_b(1/x) replacing the base or argument by its reciprocal negates the logarithm. \log_{1/b}(x) = -\log_{b}(x) = \log_{b}\!\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)

formulas.title: Number of Digits in Base-10 Representation
formulas.note: Gives the exact number of digits of any positive integer N in standard decimal notation.
formulas.search_text: logarithms laws of logarithms · change of base · exponential equivalence · characteristic & mantissa number of digits in base-10 representation d = floor(log10(n)) + 1 gives the exact number of digits of any positive integer n in standard decimal notation. d = \lfloor \log_{10}(n) \rfloor + 1

formulas.title: nth Term of an Arithmetic Progression (AP)
formulas.note: a_1 is the first term and d = a_2 - a_1 is the constant common difference.
formulas.search_text: number series arithmetic progression · geometric progression · harmonic mean · power sums nth term of an arithmetic progression (ap) a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)*d a_1 is the first term and d = a_2 - a_1 is the constant common difference. a_{n} = a_{1} + (n - 1)d

formulas.title: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
formulas.note: Equals the number of terms multiplied by the average of the first and last terms.
formulas.search_text: number series arithmetic progression · geometric progression · harmonic mean · power sums sum of first n terms of an ap s_n = (n/2)*[2*a_1 + (n - 1)*d] = (n/2)*(a_1 + a_n) equals the number of terms multiplied by the average of the first and last terms. s_{n} = \frac{n}{2}\bigl[2a_{1} + (n - 1)d\bigr] = \frac{n}{2}(a_{1} + a_{n})

formulas.title: Arithmetic Mean (AM)
formulas.note: Middle term when three quantities a, AM, b form an Arithmetic Progression.
formulas.search_text: number series arithmetic progression · geometric progression · harmonic mean · power sums arithmetic mean (am) am = (a + b) / 2 middle term when three quantities a, am, b form an arithmetic progression. \text{am} = \frac{a + b}{2}

formulas.title: nth Term of a Geometric Progression (GP)
formulas.note: a_1 is the first term and r = a_2 / a_1 is the non-zero common ratio.
formulas.search_text: number series arithmetic progression · geometric progression · harmonic mean · power sums nth term of a geometric progression (gp) a_n = a_1 * r^(n - 1) a_1 is the first term and r = a_2 / a_1 is the non-zero common ratio. a_{n} = a_{1}\,r^{n - 1}

formulas.title: Sum of First n Terms of a GP
formulas.note: For r = 1, the sum is simply S_n = n * a_1.
formulas.search_text: number series arithmetic progression · geometric progression · harmonic mean · power sums sum of first n terms of a gp s_n = a_1 * (r^n - 1) / (r - 1) for r != 1 for r = 1, the sum is simply s_n = n * a_1. s_{n} = \frac{a_{1}(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r} = \frac{a_{1}(r^{n} - 1)}{r - 1} \quad (r \neq 1)

formulas.title: Sum of an Infinite Geometric Series
formulas.note: Converges if and only if the magnitude of common ratio r is strictly less than 1.
formulas.search_text: number series arithmetic progression · geometric progression · harmonic mean · power sums sum of an infinite geometric series s_infinity = a_1 / (1 - r) for |r| < 1 converges if and only if the magnitude of common ratio r is strictly less than 1. s_{\infty} = \frac{a_{1}}{1 - r} \quad (|r| < 1)

formulas.title: Geometric Mean (GM)
formulas.note: For n positive numbers, GM = (x_1 * x_2 * ... * x_n)^(1/n).
formulas.search_text: number series arithmetic progression · geometric progression · harmonic mean · power sums geometric mean (gm) gm = sqrt(a * b) for n positive numbers, gm = (x_1 * x_2 * ... * x_n)^(1/n). \text{gm} = \sqrt{ab} \quad (a, b > 0)

formulas.title: Harmonic Mean (HM) of Two Numbers
formulas.note: Reciprocal of the arithmetic mean of the reciprocals. Also gives average speed over equal distances.
formulas.search_text: number series arithmetic progression · geometric progression · harmonic mean · power sums harmonic mean (hm) of two numbers hm = (2 * a * b) / (a + b) reciprocal of the arithmetic mean of the reciprocals. also gives average speed over equal distances. \text{hm} = \frac{2ab}{a + b}

formulas.title: Sum of First n Natural Numbers
formulas.note: Triangular number formula for the sum of the first n positive integers.

formulas.title: Sum of Squares of First n Natural Numbers

formulas.title: Sum of Cubes of First n Natural Numbers

formulas.search_text: number series arithmetic progression · geometric progression · harmonic mean · power sums sum of cubes of first n natural numbers sum(k^3, k=1..n) = (n*(n + 1) / 2)^2 equals the square of the sum of the first n natural numbers. \sum_{k=1}^{n} k^{3} = \left[\frac{n(n + 1)}{2}\right]^{2}

formulas.title: Sum of First n Odd Natural Numbers
formulas.note: The sum of the first n odd positive integers is always a perfect square n^2.
